page: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v7 is an ARM64-based virtual machine configured under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by 32 dedicated 64-bit ARM vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core. As a member of Azure's low-memory, local-disk ARM series, the hardware configuration targets compute tasks that do not require standard or memory-optimized memory footprints.

A key hardware element of the D32plds_v7 is its integrated local NVMe SSD storage, providing 1888 GB of high-speed temporary storage directly attached to the host. The instance does not include dedicated graphics processing units, functioning strictly as a general compute node with premium storage support. It includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring virtual network routing or external IP assignment for external connectivity.

Cost efficiency for this instance is driven by its high core density, ARM architecture efficiency, and bundled high-capacity NVMe drive. Deployments requiring significant local read/write caches avoid the supplemental expense of provisioning separate high-IOPS external disk attachments. However, the reduced memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU represents an architectural tradeoff, making the instance less practical for memory-heavy databases or caching layers.

The D32plds_v7 is well aligned with multi-threaded, parallel processing workloads requiring rapid local temporary storage. Representative use cases include distributed build pipelines, CI/CD compilation runners, batch data transformations, video transcode processing, and application worker pools compatible with the ARM64 ecosystem.
description: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v7 is a 64-bit ARM-based virtual machine designed for compute-centric workloads requiring high-speed local disk capacity. The configuration supplies 32 dedicated ARM vCPUs paired with 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. In addition to premium storage capability, the instance features an integrated 1888 GB NVMe SSD for high-throughput local scratch space and temporary caching. Operating without hardware GPU acceleration under Microsoft Hyper-V, the architecture emphasizes processing density and cost efficiency derived from ARM microarchitectures. The reduced memory ratio makes it an economical choice for multi-threaded processes that do not mandate large memory pools. Primary workload fits include code compilation pipelines, batch processing engines, media encoding, and ARM-native backend services.
